name: Sparse DETR
main_result: Swin-T Deformable DETR COCO: AP 48.2 at 113 GFLOPs / 21.2 FPS (baseline 48.0 at 185 GFLOPs / 15.4 FPS), keep ratio 10%
notes: Tokens are the multi-scale backbone features entering the Deformable DETR encoder. Unselected tokens are not updated but pass through every encoder layer and serve as keys, so no reactivation is needed for the decoder. A 4-layer scoring network is trained with BCE against the binarized decoder cross-attention map (DAM); an objectness-score variant is also reported. The whole detector is trained for 50 epochs with the Deformable DETR recipe (ImageNet-pretrained backbone). FPS measured as in Deformable DETR; batch size for FPS not stated.
evidence: "For features that are not updated in this process, the values of xfeat are passed through the encoder layers without being changed." (Sec. 3.2); "we consider a 4-layer scoring network g to predict how likely a given encoder token is included in the top-ρ % most referenced tokens, and the network is trained by minimizing the binary cross entropy (BCE) loss between the binarized DAM and prediction" (Sec. 3.3); "We then define ρ-salient regions Ωρs as the top-ρ% tokens with the highest scores, for a given keeping ratio ρ" (Sec. 3.2); "We train the model on a 4×V100 GPU machine with a total batch size of 16, for 50 epochs" (Sec. 4)

name: Focus-DETR
backbones: ResNet-50; ResNet-101; Swin-T (DINO / Deformable DETR encoder)
main_result: ResNet-50 DINO COCO: AP 50.4 at 154 GFLOPs / 20.0 FPS (DINO 50.9 at 279 GFLOPs / 14.2 FPS), keep ratio 0.3
notes: Encoder tokens of DINO / Deformable DETR. A Foreground Token Selector (shared MLP with top-down score modulation across scales, trained with focal loss against GT boxes) picks foreground queries; the paper says background queries are abandoned, but in Algorithm 1 all tokens stay as keys/values and only foreground tokens are updated, so the operation is halt. A multi-category score picks a few fine-grained object tokens for an extra self-attention (dual attention). Cascade: the number of foreground tokens is reduced layer by layer. The whole detector is trained for 36 epochs. FPS on V100; batch size not stated. The abstract links a torch and a mindspore version but the URLs are not in the PDF text.
evidence: "Foreground Token Selector (FTS) aims to abandon background tokens based on top-down score modulations across multi-scale features. We assign {1,0} labels to all tokens from the backbone with reference to the ground truth and predict the foreground probability." (Sec. 1); "we design the cascade structure for the encoder to reduce the number of foreground tokens layer by layer" (Sec. 4.4); "update Tf′ in Ta according to If" (Algorithm 1); "Like DETR-like detectors, our model is trained in an end-to-end manner" (Sec. 3.5)

name: CTS
backbones: ViT-Ti/16; ViT-S/16; ViT-B/16; ViT-L/16; DeiT-B/16; BEiT-B/16; BEiT-L (Segmenter, UPerNet decoders)
main_result: Segmenter ViT-S/16 ADE20K: mIoU 45.1 at 162 im/s (baseline 45.0 at 122 im/s), 30% fewer tokens
notes: Reduction happens before the ViT. An EfficientNet-Lite0 policy network, trained separately on a binary label derived from the GT masks, predicts whether a 2x2 superpatch holds one class; the S highest-scoring superpatches are bilinearly downsampled to one patch and embedded as one token (M = N - 3S). Unsharing (reactivate): the shared token or its prediction is bilinearly upsampled to the 2x2 positions, before a CNN decoder or after a transformer decoder. The segmentation network is then trained with CTS using the original recipe. Throughput on A100 with batch 32. A per-image dynamic S is explored in Sec. 5.5 (+0.7 mIoU) but is not the main setting.
evidence: "each superpatch that can share a token according to policy P is bilinearly downsampled to the dimensions of a single patch, and linearly projected into a single token" (Sec. 3.2); "tu first unshares the shared tokens by bilinearly upsampling and rearranging them to produce L" (Sec. 3.2); "From the output of the network, the S highest-scoring superpatches are selected to share a token, to end up with M = N − 3S tokens that are processed by the transformer-based network." (Sec. 3.3); "Once the policy network is trained, we integrate it in the segmentation model and run the whole model end-to-end" (Sec. 4.3)

name: DToP
main_result: SETR ViT-B ADE20K: mIoU 47.0 at 80.6 GFLOPs (baseline 47.0 at 107.7 GFLOPs), p0 = 0.98
notes: Early exit of tokens. At fixed stages (after layers 6 and 8 for ViT-B, 8 and 16 for ViT-L) the inherent auxiliary segmentation head (ATM or FCN) grades every token; tokens whose max class probability is at least p0 get their prediction finalized from that head and leave the sequence (no reconstruction, the stage predictions are combined); the top-k (k = 5) most confident tokens of each present class are kept for context. The count varies per image, so average GFLOPs over the validation set are reported. Training variants: DToP@Direct (no training), DToP@Finetune (segmentation heads fine-tuned 40k iterations, adopted), DToP@Retrain (160k). Only FLOPs reported. No code link in the paper; the ALGM paper states that DToP did not release code.
evidence: "Easy tokens are halted and pruned early on in the ViT, while hard ones are kept to be computed in the following layers." (Sec. 1); "we prune the n-th token in Zlm if pm,n ⩾ p0 , otherwise we keep it. After propagating an image through the whole network, we combine the predicted token labels from each stage to form the final results." (Sec. 3.2); "DToP@Finetune means finetuning the segmentation heads for 40k iterations on the baseline model using DToP, and DToP@Retrain retraining the entire model using DToP for 160k iterations." (Sec. 4.3.1)

name: SViT
main_result: DeiT-S ViT-Adapter Mask R-CNN COCO: box AP 48.2 / mask AP 42.5 at 15.75 FPS (dense 48.5 / 42.8 at 11.70 FPS), A100 batch 1
notes: Pruned tokens are preserved in the feature map (used by the detection head) and can be reactivated by the gating MLP of any later layer. A 2-layer MLP with Gumbel softmax before each of blocks 4-12 decides per token; target keep ratios 70/49/34.3% are enforced by a loss averaged over the batch, so the count varies per image (dynamic rate). Detector fine-tuned 6 (tiny) / 4 (small) epochs after dense training. ImageNet numbers (Table 6) after a 30-epoch fine-tune from DeiT-S; throughput 2246 vs 1524 img/s on A100 with batch 512. Detection FPS on A100 with batch 1 (nested tensors not used for detection).
evidence: "tokens should not be completely pruned and discarded, but rather preserved in the feature maps for later use. (ii) reactivating previously pruned tokens can further enhance model performance. (iii) a dynamic pruning rate based on images is better than a fixed pruning rate. (iv) a lightweight, 2-layer MLP can effectively prune tokens" (Abstract); "For controlling the number of pruned tokens, similar to [32], we use a dynamic pruning ratio loss during training" (Sec. 3.3); "Then we finetune each sparse model for 6 and 4 epochs for tiny and small models, respectively" (Sec. 4)

name: ALGM
backbones: ViT-T; ViT-S; ViT-B; ViT-L (Segmenter, SETR, SegViT); EVA (ViT-Adapter + Mask2Former)
main_result: Segmenter ViT-S ADE20K: mIoU 46.4 at 192 im/s, 26.3 GFLOPs (baseline 45.3 at 134 im/s, 38.6 GFLOPs); ALGM* 45.5 at 235 im/s, 20.9 GFLOPs
notes: Layer 1: CLAP average-pools the tokens of each 2x2 window whose mean pairwise cosine similarity exceeds tau. Layer 5 (7 for ViT-L): GBM, ToMe bipartite matching that keeps only edges above tau. tau = mean + std of token similarities on the training set, so the token count varies per image (ALGM* uses a lower tau at inference). Unmerging duplicates the merged embedding to the original indices, before a CNN decoder or after a transformer decoder. Main results re-train the segmentation network with ALGM; a training-free application to EVA + Mask2Former keeps mIoU at +26% throughput. Throughput on A100 with batch 32.
evidence: "CLAP merges only the tokens in windows w for which µw > τ , where τ is an automatically determined similarity threshold" (Sec. 3.3); "we deploy an unmerging module that duplicates the embeddings of the merged tokens at the indices of the tokens from which they were merged" (Sec. 3.3); "Using this threshold, the number of remaining tokens N ′ and N ′′ after the CLAP and GBM modules will vary per image." (Sec. 3.3); "The results in Tab. 4 show that without training, we can improve the throughput by 26% while keeping the mIoU constant. When we also train the model, we achieve the same efficiency gains but now also further improve the mIoU with +0.2." (Sec. 5.2)

name: TORE
backbones: METRO and FastMETRO transformers with ResNet-50, HRNet-W64, EfficientNet-b0 CNN backbones
main_result: FastMETRO-R50 Human3.6M: PA-MPJPE 40.5 mm at 5.3 GFLOPs / 794.7 im/s (baseline 37.3 at 10.9 GFLOPs / 576.0 im/s), GTR + ITP@20%
notes: Human mesh recovery from a single image (target other). GTR: the transformer queries only the 14 joint tokens instead of joints plus 431 vertex tokens; a light Neural Shape Regressor recovers the vertices from the joint features (operation other). ITP: a learnable Conv + MLP + softmax map M folds the HW CNN feature tokens into T = floor(rho * HW) cluster tokens (TokenLearner-like resampling), trained with a projection-mask loss. The model is trained for 60 (FastMETRO) or 200 (METRO) epochs with an ImageNet-pretrained CNN. Throughput on RTX 3090 with batch 32 (FastMETRO) or 16 (METRO).
evidence: "Let 0 < ρ < 1 denote the predefined token pruning ratio. Our goal is to learn a projection that maps feature map FI ∈ RHW ×c extracted from the given image with HW tokens to ZI ∈ RT ×c with T tokens, where T = ⌊ρHW ⌋" (Sec. 3.2); "Inspired by [16, 59], we implement the projection as a learnable CNN module." (Sec. 3.2); "our approach only queries the body tokens, whose count is equivalent to the number of joints" (Sec. 3.1); "We use the AdamW optimizer [45] and train for 60 epochs, with a batch size of 16 per GPU on 4 Nvidia A100 GPUs." (Sec. 4.2)

name: STTS
main_result: MViT-B16 Kinetics-400: top-1 78.1 at 0.28 TFLOPs (baseline 78.4 at 0.35 TFLOPs); single view 56.4 GFLOPs at 96.5 video/s (baseline 70.5 GFLOPs at 79.3 video/s)
notes: Tokens are the 3D cube embeddings of MViT / VideoSwin. Temporal selection keeps the top-K frames (frame scores from spatially pooled tokens); spatial selection keeps one anchor region per frame so the 2D structure survives pooling. The scorer is a 2-layer MLP trained end-to-end with a perturbed-maximum differentiable Top-K; the selection ratio is fixed. Pretrained backbone fine-tuned (20 epochs for MViT, backbone lr 0.01x of the modules). Throughput measured on an 8x RTX 3090 server; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we formulate token selection as a ranking problem, which estimates the importance of each token through a lightweight scorer network and only those with top scores will be used for downstream evaluation" (Abstract); "This also allows us to explicitly control how many tokens are used." (Sec. 1); "In our experiments, we finetune the pre-trained video transformers with our STTS modules." (Sec. 4.1)

name: STA
main_result: ViT-L (VideoMAE) Kinetics-400: top-1 85.0 at 308 GFLOPs per view (baseline 85.1 at 597 GFLOPs), STA64; ViT-H 86.1 at 611 GFLOPs (86.3 at 1192)
notes: Tokens are 3D tube embeddings (2x16x16 for ViT). A constant number r of tokens per frame is dropped at three stages with a decreasing schedule (e.g. 8x64, 8x32, 8x16 for ViT-L). Score: frame-to-frame affinity of attention keys accumulated along time as a Markov chain (temporal redundancy), reweighted by one minus the normalized L1 activation sum (semantic importance); the first frame is pruned with ToMe-style similarity. For VideoSwin the dropped positions are filled with the nearest kept tokens inside window attention. Throughput in clips/s on a V100 32G with batch 32.
evidence: "Based on the STA score, we are able to progressively prune the tokens without introducing any additional parameters or requiring further re-training." (Abstract); "For simplicity, we reduce a constant number of tokens in each frame to ensure parallel computing." (Sec. 3.2); "Note that we do not need to train a new projection head f because the self-attention provides the necessary functionality, and the key function fK extracts most relevant knowledge for affinity estimation" (Sec. 3.2); "Intuitively, through the summation of absolute activation values over channel dimension, a high absolute activation suggests a significant contribution to next layers." (Sec. 3.2)

name: TESTA
backbones: ViT-B/16 video encoder (BLIP initialization, divided space-time attention)
main_result: TESTA ViT-B/16 QuerYD paragraph-to-video retrieval (32 frames): R@1 77.0 at 420 GFLOPs (without aggregation 79.7 at 786 GFLOPs)
notes: Tokens are 16x16 patch tokens per frame plus pseudo frame tokens (mean of a frame's patches). Each video encoder block merges RT frames (temporal) and RS patches per frame (spatial) by bipartite matching on the cosine similarity of attention keys and averages the features; geometry-based (alternating) partition is the default, an importance-based partition (attention received) is a variant. Aggregation runs during pre-training (5M pairs) and fine-tuning. Efficiency is reported as GFLOPs and GPU memory only; the 1.7x in the abstract is FLOPs. Findings of EMNLP 2023, pages 932-947 (no arXiv id in the list).
evidence: "TESTA condenses video semantics by adaptively aggregating similar frames, as well as similar patches within each frame." (Abstract); "For each token in the set A, we find its most similar token from the set B, then merge them by averaging their features." (Sec. 3.2.2); "After each aggregation, TAM reduces RT frames while SAM reduce RS patches, where RT and RS are hyper-parameters to control the trade-offs between performance and efficiency." (Sec. 3.2); "We conduct our aggregation during both training and testing." (Sec. 3.2.2)

name: vid-TLDR
main_result: UMT-B MSRVTT text-video retrieval: R@1 50.8 at 178.0 GFLOPs (baseline 50.0 at 303.3 GFLOPs)
notes: Tokens are the tube embeddings of the video encoder (UMT). ToMe bipartite soft matching in the first four layers. Saliency is the normalized negative entropy (sharpness) of each token's attention row, no class token needed; tokens below the mean saliency get mass 0 in the weighted average, so background tokens are effectively dropped (the paper calls it a combination of merging and pruning). A fixed number of tokens is merged per video (per-dataset numbers in the supplement). Only FLOPs reported.
evidence: "we propose training-free token merging for lightweight video Transformer (vid-TLDR) that aims to enhance the efficiency of video Transformers by merging the background tokens without additional training" (Abstract); "we devise a sharpness function S to capture the saliency of tokens with entropy" (Sec. 3.1); "Although the same number of tokens are merged in each video, we dynamically adjust the influence of uninformative tokens by suppressing the mess" (Sec. 3.2)

main_result: ViViT-B Kinetics-400: top-1 63.08 at 260.72 FPS, 2.46x (baseline 63.43 at 106.00 FPS), r = 300 tokens per layer
notes: No method name; an empirical study of ToMe on video. Joint space-time models (ViViT, VideoMAE) merge tokens across all frames by bipartite matching on key cosine similarity with proportional attention; divided space-time models (TimeSformer, Motionformer) merge per frame. Constant, increasing and decreasing r schedules; default merges 10% of the original tokens per layer (60% in total). One view per clip. GPU and batch size for the FPS numbers are not stated (fine-tuning used GH200 GPUs). SSv2 and EPIC-KITCHENS drop far more than K400 for the divided models.
evidence: "we explore the implementation of token merging in the video domain without fine-tuning, allowing tokens to merge freely in and between frames" (Sec. 1); "The similarity is defined as the cosine distance between the keys (K) of two tokens from the Query-Key-Value self-attention and this is used as the edge weighting in G." (Sec. 3.1); "We define a hyperparameter for the number of tokens to merge as ri , where 0 ≤ ri ≤ SiV /2, which represents the number of tokens to merge within the ith layer." (Sec. 3.1)

name: ToMe for SD
backbones: Stable Diffusion v1.5 (U-Net with transformer blocks)
main_result: Stable Diffusion v1.5 512x512 (ImageNet-class prompts): FID 33.37 at 1.52 s/im (baseline 33.12 at 3.09 s/im), r = 60%, RTX 4090
notes: Tokens are latent patches inside the U-Net transformer blocks of Stable Diffusion. r% of the tokens are merged before the self-attention of the highest-resolution blocks (bipartite matching on the block input x, one dst token sampled per 2x2 region with randomness fixed across the batch) and unmerged right after by copying the merged token back to both positions, so every token is restored for the next module. A linear schedule over diffusion steps (more merging early) gives little gain. Time averaged over 2000 samples on one 4090; batch size not stated.
evidence: "our ToMe for Stable Diffusion can reduce the number of tokens in an existing Stable Diffusion model by up to 60% while still producing high quality images without any extra training" (Abstract); "Instead, we'd like to merge tokens, do some (now reduced) computation, and then unmerge them afterward so we don't lose any tokens." (Sec. 3.2); "Thus instead of removing a quantity of tokens r, we remove a percentage (r%) of all tokens." (Sec. 3.2); "we don't use proportional attention and use the input to the block x for similarly rather than attention keys k" (Sec. 3.2)

name: AT-EDM
main_result: SD-XL 1024x1024 MS-COCO 2017 (5k captions): FID 28.04 / CLIP 0.3209 at 4.1 TFLOPs per step (SD-XL 31.94 / 0.3284 at 6.7 TFLOPs); sampling 20.3 s vs 31.0 s without fused ops (1.53x)
notes: Tokens are latent feature-map tokens of the SD-XL U-Net attention blocks. Importance via G-WPR, a weighted PageRank over the self-attention map (no class token, hence cls-attention in the sense of attention statistics); the top-k tokens are kept after the first attention layer of each block (pruning ratio rho = 63% for the 4.1T budget). Before each ResNet block the pruned tokens are refilled by copying the retained token from which they receive the highest attention (similarity-based copy). DSAP: in the first 15 of 50 denoising steps the first down-stage and last up-stage attention blocks are left unpruned. With xFormers the speed-up is 15-18% because attention maps must be recomputed. Batch size for latency not stated.
evidence: "leverages attention maps to perform run-time pruning of redundant tokens, without the need for any retraining. Specifically, for single-denoising-step pruning, we develop a novel ranking algorithm, Generalized Weighted Page Rank (G-WPR), to identify redundant tokens, and a similarity-based recovery method to restore tokens for the convolution operation" (Abstract); "we only insert a pruning layer after the first attention layer of each attention block and set the pruning ratio for that layer to ρ. To meet the FLOPs budget of 4.1T, we set ρ = 63%." (Sec. 4.1); "We use the self-attention map to determine the source of the highest attention received for each pruned token and use that as the most similar one." (Sec. 3.2)

backbones: Stable Diffusion 2 (U-Net); PixArt-alpha (DiT); Zero123++ (multi-view); AnimateDiff v3 (video)
main_result: Stable Diffusion 2 768x768 MS-COCO 2014 (30k): FID 17.75 / CLIP 31.76 at r = 0.75 (ToMeSD 20.89 / 31.71; no merging 11.88 / 31.83); 5.8 s vs 8.5 s per image at r = 0.7 (A5000)
notes: No acronym (importance-based token merging). Tokens are the latent tokens of the diffusion backbone (U-Net transformer blocks or DiT layers; spatial and temporal attention layers for AnimateDiff). Importance = magnitude of the classifier-free guidance term from the previous timestep (no extra cost); the top (1-r)(1+p) tokens form a pool from which dst tokens are sampled and independent tokens are chosen, all other tokens are merged into their most similar dst token (bipartite soft matching, cosine similarity, averaging); merged locations are refilled with the processed dst tokens after the layer. Cross-attention maps work as an alternative importance. Latency equals ToMeSD. No code URL found in the paper text; batch size not stated.
evidence: "we propose an importance-based token merging method that prioritizes the most critical tokens in computational resource allocation, leveraging readily available importance scores, such as those from classifier-free guidance in diffusion models" (Abstract); "Next, we perform bipartite soft matching by computing pairwise cosine similarities between src and dst tokens." (Sec. 3); "The diffusion model layer then processes this reduced token set, the merged locations are filled with the corresponding processed dst tokens, maintaining the same output shape as the input." (Sec. 3); "The token merging ratio is r." (Sec. 3)

name: DyDiT
main_result: DiT-XL ImageNet 256x256: FID 2.07 at 57.88 GFLOPs, 5.91 s/image (DiT-XL 2.27 at 118.69 GFLOPs, 10.22 s/image), lambda = 0.5, 1.73x on V100
notes: Tokens are the latent image patches of the DiT. Spatial-wise Dynamic Token (SDT): a per-layer token router (linear + sigmoid, threshold 0.5; Gumbel-sigmoid and straight-through in training) lets easy tokens bypass only the MLP block; they stay in the sequence and in self-attention (gather / scatter), so the operation is halt. Also Timestep-wise Dynamic Width (head and channel-group routing per timestep), which is not a token method. A FLOPs-constrained loss drives the average cost to a target ratio lambda; the per-image count still varies. Fine-tuned from pretrained DiT with under 3% extra iterations (48k iterations, batch 256 for XL). Speed on a V100 32G with the optimal batch size per model. arXiv Oct 2024; the key uses 2025.
evidence: "we develop a Spatial-wise Dynamic Token (SDT) strategy, which identifies image patches where noise prediction is relatively "easy", allowing them to bypass computationally intensive blocks" (Sec. 1); "Therefore, SDT is applied only in MLP blocks in each layer." (Sec. 3.3); "We then convert it into a binary mask Mtoken using a threshold of 0.5." (Sec. 3.3); "Our DyDiT can be built easily by fine-tuning on pre-trained DiT weights." (Sec. 4)

main_result: PlainMamba-L3 ImageNet-1k: top-1 81.7 at 8.44 GFLOPs, 1.43x throughput (baseline 82.3 at 14.4 GFLOPs); ViM-S 78.8 at 3.60 GFLOPs (80.5 at 5.10)
notes: No method name (models are called -prune). SSM backbone without attention. Importance = mean over channels of the clipped SSM output max(0, y), which beats l1 / l2 norms. Pruning-aware hidden state alignment: pruned tokens are removed from the computation but their scan positions are kept, the hidden state at a pruned position is advanced as h <- A h, so the neighbourhood of the kept tokens is unchanged; a custom scan kernel implements it. Pruning after fixed layers (ViM-S: 5, 10, 15, 20; PlainMamba-L3: 5, 11, 17, 23); the per-layer keep ratio is not stated, only the resulting FLOPs. 30-epoch fine-tuning. Also COCO (Mask R-CNN / RetinaNet with ViT-Adapter) and ADE20K. Throughput is given as a ratio only; the GPU for it is not stated (experiments on V100). No code link in the paper.
evidence: "we aggregate the clipped values across all channels for each token to evaluate token importance" (Sec. 4.2); "if a token is pruned, we do not simply remove its corresponding hidden state during the scan as it leads to substantial accuracy degradation shown in Figure 1 and 2. Instead, its hidden state in the scan can be obtained by using the previous state with one step forward" (Sec. 4.1); "For ViM-S, we prune after the 5th, 10th, 15th, and 20th layers." (Sec. 5); "We finetune both the ViM and PlainMamba for 30 epochs on the ImageNet-1K dataset." (Sec. 5.1)

name: MTR
main_result: ViM-B ImageNet-1k: top-1 80.3 at 40% FLOPs reduction (baseline 81.9); ViM-S 75.4 at 40% reduction (80.5)
notes: SSM backbone without attention. Importance = the selective-SSM timescale parameter Delta_t, summed over scan heads and averaged over channels (no extra cost; beats B_t, C_t, hidden state and [CLS] similarity). Tokens are sorted by importance into keep (k%), target (1 - 2k%) and source (k%) groups; source tokens are merged into their most similar target token (bipartite matching, mean) and the remaining tokens are reordered to their original positions, which matters for Mamba. k is fixed across layers and set by the FLOPs target. Throughput only as a figure (Fig. 4) without GPU or batch size (experiments on V100). Absolute GFLOPs are not given, only reduction ratios. No code link in the paper.
evidence: "we found that the timescale parameter ∆ in Mamba effectively serves this purpose" (Sec. Introduction); "Tokens in the ’source’ group are merged with those in the ’target’ group, while the critical tokens in the ’keep’ group remain unchanged." (Sec. Methodology); "Finally, the remaining tokens are reordered according to their original sequential positions." (Sec. Methodology); "the grouping ratio k is fixed across all layers" (Sec. Methodology); "Without the need for training or additional tuning parameters, our method can be seamlessly integrated as a plug-and-play component across various Mamba models." (Abstract)
